articles.title: Stokes registers for 2027 IPL auction
articles.summary: Former England captain Ben ‌Stokes has registered for the 2027 Indian ‌Premier League auction, Cricinfo reported ​on Tuesday, with the all-rounder among the long list of names potentially set to go under the hammer in ‌Goa on December 16.
body: IPL rules barred players ​who skipped the mega auction in 2025 from registering for the ​following mini auction, ⁠meaning Stokes could ⁠not return to the auction pool until ‌2027.
Indian media reported, however, that the 35-year-old has been ‌granted permission by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) to enter this ⁠year's auction.

The 35-year-old has been listed at the maximum base price of INR 2 crore [£165,000] with the players' auction held next month, a day before England's first Test on their tour of South Africa, live on Sky Sports.
England internationals Jonny Bairstow, Sam Billings, Sonny Baker and Tom Curran are also in the 30-player group with the maximum base price.

articles.title: Sinner surgery casts doubt over Australian Open appearance
articles.summary: Former world No 1 Jannik Sinner has undergone surgery on his troublesome knee, casting doubt over his hopes of playing at the Australian Open.
body: The 25-year-old has not played since ​winning his fifth Grand Slam ‌title at Wimbledon in July.
The Italian world No 2 ​said this month he was confident of returning in time for the Australian Open, which starts on January ​17, but would not rush his ⁠recovery.
Sky Italy are reporting he could be out for up to three months.

Five-time Grand Slam champion Sinner posted on social media: "Over the past few months, together with my team we've tried everything to treat my injury without surgery. After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn't respond as we'd all hoped, that's why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band.

articles.title: Sheehan out of Wallabies Test after two-game ban
articles.summary: Ireland's stand-in captain Dan Sheehan will be banned for two games after a croc-roll tackle against South Africa and will play no part against Australia on Friday night.
body: The Leinster forward was shown a yellow card by referee Christophe Ridley in the 72nd minute of Ireland's 20-17 victory over the Springboks in Dublin on Saturday.

That was later upgraded to a red card by the foul play review officer (FPRO) on the basis of World Rugby's Law 9.20d that "a player may remove the jackler from the tackle area by pushing/driving them backwards (including by grabbing the knee/leg), but must not roll, pull or twist an opponent".
The 28-year-old faced a disciplinary hearing on Monday evening where the panel found that the incident was a "low-entry point" offence and merited a two-week ban.

Sheehan will miss Friday's Nations Championship finals weekend fixture against Australia in Twickenham (20:10 GMT) and Leinster's game against Ospreys in the United Rugby Championship (URC) on 4 December.

articles.title: Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners - 10 months after tournament
articles.summary: Ten months after the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final, Senegal are reinstated as champions following a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
body: The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January.

With the game goalless, Senegal left the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. The match in Rabat was delayed by over 15 minutes before Morocco's Brahim Diaz had his spot-kick saved.
Senegal then triumphed 1-0 after extra time, with Pape Gueye scoring the winner.

That result was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed the Teranga Lions had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play after the penalty was awarded.

articles.title: How 'quick check' and unseen angle saw Timber's Isak shirt-pull go unpunished
articles.summary: Referees’ chief Howard Webb admitted it was a “quick check” by VAR for Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber’s unpunished shirt-pull on Liverpool striker Alexander Isak in the Gunners’ win at Anfield.
body: Webb also said Isak's lack of a "natural reaction" to Timber's shirt pull on him was a factor in the decision not to award a penalty after the striker did not go down or protest the decision.
Earlier this month, the Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel ruled Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty for Timber's shirt tug on Isak inside the box at a cross.
Upon a review of the incident on Match Officials Mic'd Up, it was revealed that VAR Stuart Attwell spotted the shirt-pull offence but decided it was "all fine" 11 seconds later.

After declaring it was "all fine", referee Andy Madley and the assistant referee asked for clarification, which Attwell immediately responded to with "all fine", meaning the total check took only 18 seconds.

articles.title: Defender Heaven open to leaving Man Utd
articles.summary: Manchester United defender Ayden Heaven is open to a loan move in January amid concerns over his game time as his side battles in the Premier League relegation zone.
body: The 20-year-old centre-back is concerned about what United's current situation means for his development, after new manager Mauricio Pochettino left him as an unused substitute in Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool.
Now on his third manager in 21 months since joining from Arsenal in February 2025, Heaven accepts Pochettino may prefer more experienced options as United attempt to avoid a shock relegation.
The club have also been heavily linked with signing a centre-back in the coming January window, with targets said to include Fulham 's Calvin Bassey.
However, the Cottagers regard Bassey as an important player and would not encourage any interest.

articles.title: Sooryavanshi, 15, breaks sixes record by scoring 204 off 53 balls
articles.summary: India's 15-year-old sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi blazes 204 from 53 balls for India A, almost halving the record for the fastest double-century in List A cricket.
body: India's 15-year-old batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit the most sixes ever recorded in a senior men's innings in blazing 204 from 53 balls for India A against the United Arab Emirates.
The teenage opener also broke the record for the fastest century and 150, the latter of which he already held, before being caught at long-off with his side five runs from victory.
India A ultimately passed their target of 250, played against a UAE side that featured a number of internationals but was not their current first-choice side, in 14.2 overs in Doha.

The previous record for the most sixes in senior matches was 26, struck by Tanmay Agarwal in an innings of 366 for Hyderabad against Arunachal Pradesh in India's first-class Ranji Trophy competition in January 2024.

articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers will continue their annual tradition of signing autographs to raise money for Salvation Army's Red Kettle campaign during this holiday season. Players will sign autographs from 5-6 p.m. on Nov. 30, Dec. 7 and Dec. 14 in the Lambeau Field Atrium.
body: The first to sign autographs will be cornerback Brandon Cisse, edge rusher Brenton Cox Jr., quarterback Tyrod Taylor, running back Kaleb Johnson and offensive lineman Jager Burton. Fans are asked to donate a minimum of $50 for the Nov. 30 session.

All proceeds go toward aiding families in need, seniors and people experiencing homelessness in the Green Bay area. Many of the organization’s programs operate only because of the money received through Red Kettle donations.
For information on The Salvation Army of Greater Green Bay, visit sagreenbay.org.

articles.title: Rob Gronkowski Among 1st-Time Eligibles Advancing In Hall of Fame Voting Process
articles.summary: Rob Gronkowski and Ben Roethlisberger are among the first-time eligible players who have advanced in the voting process for the Pro Football Hall of Fame Class of 2027. Adrian Peterson, Antonio Brown and Richard Sherman also advanced in their first year of eligibility.
body: A total of 52 players have reached this stage, including Ken Anderson and Eli Manning. The Hall of Fame selection committee will reduce the list to 25 candidates in two weeks.

Gronkowski was drafted by the New England Patriots in the second round of the 2010 NFL Draft, and in his second season was an All-Pro tight end who led the NFL in touchdown receptions with 17. Gronkowski also set what would end up being career-high marks in receiving yards (1,327) and first downs (69).

The 6-foot-6 Gronkowski would be part of four Super Bowl champions, was named an All-Pro tight end on four occasions, made five Pro Bowls and finished his career with 9,286 receiving yards and 92 touchdowns, good for sixth and third all-time despite not playing in 2019 due to retirement, then retiring once more after 2022, giving Gronkowski 11 years and 143 games in his career.

articles.title: Urban Meyer 'concerned' about state of Ohio State program ahead of showdown vs. Michigan
articles.summary: The former Buckeyes coach offered a vote of confidence for Ryan Day, but says fans have the right to 'point fingers' after a disappointing season
body: Urban Meyer never lost to Michigan during his time at Ohio State, so he knows a thing or two about getting his guys ready to play the biggest game of the Buckeyes' season.

This year's Buckeyes, fresh off their fourth loss that all but ended College Football Playoff hopes, are reeling down the stretch with a backup quarterback, inconsistency on defense and an elite coach who's facing unexpected pressure after falling well short of preseason No. 1 expectations.

"Am I concerned? I am a little bit. You just feel this (thing) around Columbus, Ohio," Meyer said this week on The Triple Option. "Who's gonna get fired? Who's not gonna get fired? Who's gonna stay? Who's in the portal? I'm hopeful that you walk into Woody Hayes facility right now and there's nothing but six straight days of 'How do you beat this team?' Am I concerned a little bit? I am. Not with the head coach, not at all.

Over the weekend, Meyer started his unofficial Michigan-Ohio State preview conversation during an event at the Fawcett Center on campus, "Scarlet & Gray Saturdays: The Ohio State Football Story," which included Jim Tressel and Archie Griffin.

articles.summary: Your trade deadline is coming soon! Use the trade chart to make post-draft deals and improve your team with assigned values to help you navigate your league's trade market
body: More than fifteen seasons ago, the Fantasy Football Trade Chart was invented by CBS Sports with the sole purpose of helping managers make fair trades in their leagues. And since then, the Trade Chart has expanded to include four-point-per-pass touchdown leagues and half-PPR leagues.

The points assigned to players below reflect a long-term measurement of their Fantasy value, which is determined by expected future performance, future schedules and (perhaps most importantly) public sentiment. Past performance is not a major factor in the Fantasy Football Trade Chart.

By adding players' values, you can determine what players you should be able to get in return. The higher the value, the better the player's value. However, Fantasy managers should deduct 10% of the value from any trade where one side has two or more players than the other. Also, a handful of others only carry legitimate value in two-QB or full-PPR leagues (and thus have no value listed in one-QB or non-PPR leagues).
This list also works as a "rest-of-season" rankings for the 2026 campaign.
